history.dynasty: Modern - built by the Kalinga Cultural Trust (Hyderabad's Oriya/Odia community), 21st century
history.period: Constructed 2007-2009; opened to the public March 2009
history.summary: The Jagannath Temple on Road No. 12, Banjara Hills (Bhavani Nagar), Hyderabad, is a modern replica of the Puri Jagannath Temple in Odisha. It was built by the Kalinga Cultural Trust of Hyderabad (the city's Oriya community) and opened to the public in March 2009. The red-sandstone complex spreads over about 10.7 acres and is 72 ft high (compared to Puri's 214 ft); it replicates the Puri plan with Garbha Gruha, Jagan Mohan, dancing hall and Bhoga Mandap, with mythological murals carved on the boundary walls. The main deities - Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra - are wooden idols like those at Puri; the five sub-shrine deities are stone. The complex also has the 'Chakadola' light-and-sound show on the emergence of the Jagannath cult (introduced 2018) and a 3D projection mapping show on weekends. CONFLICT NOTE FOR REVIEW: the batch brief described this row as 'the ISKCON Jagannath at Banjara Hills'. No web source consulted supports that: the Banjara Hills Jagannath temple is consistently attributed to the Kalinga Cultural Trust / Oriya community, while Hyderabad's ISKCON temple is the Sri Sri Radha Madanmohan Mandir at Nampally Station Road, Abids (a separate temple, not on Road No. 12 Banjara Hills). The file documents the well-established Kalinga Cultural Trust temple as the best-supported referent; if the CSV row intended a different shrine, the row needs correction.
